metadata.name: Adolf Hitler
metadata.description: Nazi dictator of Germany whose regime pursued racial persecution, genocide and wars of conquest.
metadata.scope: Personal positions and governing conduct during 1933–1945; earlier writings are contextual only. Historical analogies to contemporary technologies are explicitly inferred, not claims that the subject answered a modern questionnaire. Coalition constraints and contradictions are identified by axis.

axes.counterEvidence: Plebiscites and retained institutions ratified leadership decisions; they were not competitive checks.

Experts advised the leader rather than selecting government.

Plebiscitary mobilisation did not permit representative recall.

axes.counterEvidence: Regime discretion could tolerate approved activities; that is distinct from a universal legal liberty.

Universal firearm access contradicts exclusion of targeted populations.

axes.brief: Racial eligibility and state permission dominated admission, settlement and expulsion.
axes.counterEvidence: Importation of forced labour was coercion, not support for immigration rights.

answers.rationale: Strict controls compatible with racial demographic planning.
General right to improve circumstances rejected for excluded groups.

Racial selection and state authorisation were fundamental, while employment or family links could be useful without defining a universal sponsorship requirement. Strong administrative control alone does not establish this particular admission mechanism.
Academic achievement cannot substitute for racial eligibility.
Persecution does not override racial admission barriers.
Selected culturally German populations received priority.
Universal non-citizen provision conflicts with exclusionary welfare.
Diversity itself was viewed as undesirable.

axes.brief: Rearmament and aggressive expansion required armed superiority and expeditionary war.
axes.counterEvidence: Diplomatic agreements bought advantage and time; they did not establish a defence-only doctrine.

answers.rationale: Wars of expansion plainly exceed defensive response.
Negotiation subordinate to military territorial objectives.

Initiative in conflict supports pre-emptive attack.

axes.brief: International commitments were subordinate to unilateral German power.
axes.counterEvidence: Axis alliance and tactical pacts show cooperation without acceptance of superior international authority.

answers.rationale: German leadership claims ultimate domestic jurisdiction.

Military alliances were useful, but Hitler repeatedly subordinated allied coordination to unilateral German decisions. An alliance requiring one binding common foreign policy conflicts with that retained freedom.

Pooling permitted instrumentally, not equal shared sovereignty.
Borders and settlement exclusively subject to Reich control.
Bilateral deals useful but national discretion prioritised.

axes.brief: Religious institutions were accommodated and controlled, while political law derived from racial-state authority.

axes.brief: Rearmament and synthetic production favoured rapid technological deployment; biomedical policy was coercive and racially differentiated.
axes.counterEvidence: Experiments on persecuted prisoners cannot alone prove willingness to risk healthy favoured citizens; enhancement items therefore balance utility with racial-health protection.

answers.rationale: Memorandum rejects technological delay despite unresolved processes. Historical analogy, not a recorded answer to this modern proposal.
Long precautionary trials conflict with urgent deployment. Historical analogy, not a recorded answer to this modern proposal.
Strategic infrastructure outweighs habitat loss. Historical analogy, not a recorded answer to this modern proposal.
Medical utility could outweigh long follow-up requirements. Historical analogy, not a recorded answer to this modern proposal.
Labour mobilisation would accept productivity technology and retraining. Historical analogy, not a recorded answer to this modern proposal.
Preservation cannot veto national productive needs. Historical analogy, not a recorded answer to this modern proposal.
Synthetic substitution extends plausibly to food self-sufficiency. Historical analogy, not a recorded answer to this modern proposal.
Enhancement utility conflicts with protecting favoured hereditary stock. Historical analogy, not a recorded answer to this modern proposal.
Technical production advances preferred to reducing national output. Historical analogy, not a recorded answer to this modern proposal.
Environmental uncertainty would not veto strategic construction. Historical analogy, not a recorded answer to this modern proposal.
Potential enhancement welcomed, but personal choice insufficient for state approval. Historical analogy, not a recorded answer to this modern proposal.
Utility favours deployment while failed diagnosis threatens valued population; conditional balance. Historical analogy, not a recorded answer to this modern proposal.

Selective breeding and coercive racial-health policy make state-directed hereditary enhancement a plausible analogy. They do not establish his acceptance of this particular embryo-editing technique or its safety; agreement is consequently limited, not categorical.
Yield and self-sufficiency likely override blanket ecosystem-proof demand. Historical analogy, not a recorded answer to this modern proposal.
National infrastructure expansion outranks undeveloped land. Historical analogy, not a recorded answer to this modern proposal.

The memorandum prioritises urgent strategic gains despite incomplete technical assurance. By analogy, he would be unlikely to require strong evidence that irreversible harm is unlikely before proceeding, although risk to favoured populations qualifies this inference.

review.notes: Read all 240 item rationales against the exact bank and checked all 15 briefs, counter-evidence, direction and metadata. Rechecked the 1936 economic memorandum, racial-ideology history and 1933 Concordat. Retained the important distinction between private title and compulsory economic direction, and between racially restricted welfare and universal redistribution. Corrected the religious-school item to reflect actual Concordat instruction, qualified the sponsorship inference, and separated military alliances from accepting a binding common foreign policy. Reduced categorical extrapolation on autonomous weapons and embryo enhancement to limited agreement with explicit caveats. Assessed racial beliefs are described as Nazi doctrine, not factual explanations of human traits. Modern personal-liberty and technology items remain historical analogies. Neutral religious and ownership answers represent documented institutional mixtures. Portrait and full-catalogue similarity checks follow in integration. Integration review by OpenAI Codex /root on 2026-10-04: portrait identity, local rendering, size and Commons attribution checked; the shared Image credits list includes this source. All 35 requested profiles were compared using calculated scores, with any resemblance at or above 95% explicitly reviewed against the named revision. Neutral-count warnings were retained only after the evidence review; they are not missing answers. Portrait integration review by OpenAI Codex on 2026-10-04: verified the Wikipedia infobox file, Commons creator and reuse status, and image size. The independent political evidence audit is retained; no political assessment changed.
